query: The life insurer's pricing model was examined for possible biases in its data that could lead to discrimination against applicants of one sex.
The provider of the premium-setting model took measures to detect, prevent and mitigate the biases it found.
The data used to train the underwriting model are relevant, representative and as free of errors as possible.
The pricing system is transparent enough for the underwriter to interpret why a premium was quoted and to use the output appropriately.
The premium model reaches an appropriate level of accuracy and robustness and quotes consistently throughout its lifecycle.
The rating engine is resilient to errors and inconsistencies and prevents biased quotes from feeding back into later training.
An AI system used to assess risk and set prices for individuals applying for life or health insurance is high-risk.
note: life and health insurance = high-risk (Annex III 5c)

query: Before an insurer deploys an AI system to price life and health insurance, it must assess the impact on fundamental rights.
A person whose insurance premium was set on the basis of a high-risk AI system's output can ask for a clear explanation of its role in the decision.
The insurer must keep the automatically generated logs of the pricing system and monitor it on the basis of the instructions for use.
